text: The Segal condition in simplicial type theory states: for a type A with a,b,c:A and f:hom(a,b) and g:hom(b,c), the type of composites is:
choices: contractible (unique composite exists up to homotopy)
explanation: Segal condition: Σ(h:hom(a,c)). comp(f,g,h) is contractible — there is a unique composite h = g∘f up to homotopy. This is ∞-categorical composition.
